notes.claim: The logarithm of a product is the sum of the logs of its factors.
In the log system multiplication becomes addition and division subtraction, and powers become multiplication, which is why decibel gains of stages add.
A decibel is 10 times the common logarithm of a power ratio (added for i5's decibel screens).
Engine-room sound readings are taken in decibels with A-weighting, dB(A) (added for i5's decibel screen).

sources.title: Intro to logarithm properties (article) | Khan Academy
sources.quote: This property says that the logarithm of a product is the sum of the logs of its factors.

sources.title: 1.2: The Decibel - Engineering LibreTexts
sources.quote: Normal multiplication becomes addition in the log system, and division becomes subtraction. Likewise, powers and roots become multiplication and division.

sources.title: Decibel (dB) | Definition, Formula, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: One decibel (0.1 bel) equals 10 times the common logarithm of the power ratio.

sources.title: Resolution MSC.337(91), Code on Noise Levels on Board Ships - IMO
sources.quote: 3.6.2 Sound pressure level readings shall be taken in decibels using an A-weighting (dB(A)) and C-weighting (dB(C)) filter and if necessary also in octave bands between 31.5 and 8,000 Hz.
